terms.def: A single part of an electronic circuit, such as a resistor, capacitor or transistor.
terms.more: A schematic shows accurately how components are connected.

terms.def: A component that opposes the flow of current.
terms.more: It opposes current even in a DC circuit. Its schematic symbol is a zigzag line.

terms.def: A resistor whose resistance can be adjusted, usually by turning a knob.
terms.more: Often used as a volume control. The parameter it controls is resistance. Its symbol is a resistor zigzag with an arrow.

terms.def: The opposition to the flow of current, measured in ohms.
terms.more: It is the property of a resistor, and the parameter a potentiometer controls.

terms.def: The flow of electrons through a circuit, measured in amperes.
terms.more: A resistor opposes it, a diode lets it flow in only one direction, and a transistor can control it.

terms.def: Direct current: current that flows in one direction only.
terms.more: A rectifier changes AC into a varying DC.

terms.def: Alternating current: current that keeps reversing direction.
terms.more: A transformer changes AC to a higher or lower AC voltage. A rectifier changes AC into varying DC.

terms.def: The electrical push that makes current flow, measured in volts.
terms.more: A regulator controls the voltage from a power supply. A transformer changes one AC voltage to another.

terms.def: A component made of conductive surfaces separated by an insulator, which stores energy in an electric field.
terms.more: Combined with an inductor it makes a resonant circuit. Compare the inductor, which stores energy in a magnetic field.

terms.def: A component, typically a coil of wire, that stores energy in a magnetic field.
terms.more: Combined with a capacitor it makes a resonant circuit. Compare the capacitor, which stores energy in an electric field.

terms.def: A coil whose inductance can be adjusted.
terms.more: On a schematic it is drawn as the loops of a coil with an arrow.

terms.def: The region of electrical force around charged objects, such as between the plates of a capacitor.
terms.more: A capacitor stores energy in an electric field.

terms.def: The region of magnetic force around a magnet or around a wire carrying current.
terms.more: An inductor stores energy in a magnetic field.

terms.def: A material that lets almost no current flow through it.
terms.more: A capacitor is built from conductive surfaces separated by an insulator.

terms.def: A component that opens or closes a circuit, or connects it to a different circuit.
terms.more: Switches are named by their number of poles and throws, for example SPST and SPDT.

terms.def: In a switch, a circuit that the switch controls; a single-pole switch controls one circuit.
terms.more: Single-pole (SP) means one circuit is switched; double-pole (DP) means two are switched together.

terms.def: In a switch, a position that a pole can be connected to.
terms.more: Single-throw (ST) is plain on-off. Double-throw (DT) connects the pole to one of two other circuits.

terms.def: Single-pole double-throw: a switch in which a single circuit is switched between one of two other circuits.
terms.more: Compare SPST, a plain on-off switch that only opens or closes a single circuit.

terms.def: Single-pole single-throw: a simple on-off switch that opens or closes a single circuit.
terms.more: Its symbol shows one moving arm and one contact. It is component 3 in figure T-2.

terms.def: A source of electrical energy that makes voltage by a chemical reaction.
terms.more: Some chemistries are rechargeable and some are not. Its schematic symbol is a stack of alternating long and short parallel lines.

terms.def: A battery that can be refilled with energy by passing current back into it, and then used again.
terms.more: Nickel-metal hydride, lithium-ion, lead-acid and nickel-cadmium are rechargeable. Carbon-zinc is not.

terms.def: A rechargeable battery chemistry.
A rechargeable battery chemistry.
A rechargeable battery chemistry, the kind used in car batteries.
A battery chemistry that is not rechargeable.
terms.more: It is the one to pick when asked which chemistry is not rechargeable.

terms.def: A material that conducts better than an insulator but not as well as a metal, used to make diodes, transistors and integrated circuits.
terms.more: A transistor can consist of three regions of semiconductor material.

terms.def: A component that allows current to flow in only one direction.
terms.more: Its two electrodes are the anode and the cathode. The cathode lead is often marked with a stripe on the package.

terms.def: The small voltage lost across a diode while it is conducting.
terms.more: It is lower in some diode types than in others.

terms.def: Current flowing through a diode in the direction in which it conducts.
terms.more: Forward current is what makes an LED emit light.

terms.def: A terminal through which current enters or leaves a device such as a diode or a transistor.
terms.more: Diode: anode and cathode. Bipolar junction transistor: emitter, base and collector. Field-effect transistor: gate, drain and source.

terms.def: One of the two electrodes of a diode; the other is the cathode.
terms.more: When a diode conducts, current is said to flow in at the anode and out at the cathode.

terms.def: One of the two electrodes of a diode; the other is the anode.
terms.more: The cathode lead of a semiconductor diode is often marked on the package with a stripe.

terms.def: Light-emitting diode: a diode that gives off light when forward current flows through it.
terms.more: Commonly used as a visual indicator. Its schematic symbol is a diode symbol with small arrows pointing away from it.

terms.def: A semiconductor component in which a small signal controls a larger current, so it can amplify or act as a switch.
terms.more: It can be used as an electronic switch, can provide power gain, and can consist of three regions of semiconductor material.

terms.def: Field-effect transistor: the type of transistor that has a gate, a drain and a source.
terms.more: Compare the bipolar junction transistor, whose electrodes are the emitter, base and collector.

terms.def: The names of the three electrodes of a field-effect transistor.
terms.more: Do not mix them up with emitter, base and collector, which belong to a bipolar junction transistor.

terms.def: The type of transistor whose three electrodes are called the emitter, base and collector.
terms.more: Compare the field-effect transistor (FET), which has a gate, drain and source.

terms.def: The names of the three electrodes of a bipolar junction transistor.
terms.more: Do not mix them up with gate, drain and source, which belong to a field-effect transistor.

terms.def: How much larger a signal is at the output of an amplifier than at its input.
terms.more: It can be stated as output relative to input for voltage, for current or for power. A transistor can provide power gain.

terms.def: A circuit that makes a signal larger.
terms.more: How much larger is called its gain.

terms.def: An electrical diagram that uses standard component symbols.
terms.more: It accurately shows component connections. It does not show wire lengths or what the components look like.

terms.def: A standard simple drawing that stands for one kind of component on an electrical diagram.
terms.more: Zigzag = resistor. Two facing plates = capacitor. Loops = inductor. Two coils side by side = transformer. An added arrow means variable.

terms.def: A component that gives off light when current flows through it.
terms.more: It is component 3 in figure T-1.

terms.def: A component that changes an AC voltage to a higher or lower AC voltage.
terms.more: For example it changes 120 V AC power to a lower AC voltage. Its symbol is two coils side by side.

terms.def: The part of a radio station that sends out and picks up radio waves.
terms.more: It is component 4 in figure T-3.

terms.def: A device or circuit that changes an alternating current into a varying direct current signal.
terms.more: It is built from diodes, which pass current in only one direction.

terms.def: An electrically-controlled switch.
terms.more: A current through its coil moves the switch contacts.

terms.def: Wire with a conductive layer wrapped around the inner conductor.
terms.more: It is used to prevent coupling of unwanted signals to or from the wire.

terms.def: A device that displays an electrical quantity as a numeric value.
terms.more: For example, a meter can show voltage or current.

terms.def: A circuit that controls the amount of voltage from a power supply.
A device that provides the voltage and current that equipment needs to run.
terms.more: A regulator circuit controls the amount of voltage it delivers.

terms.def: An inductor and a capacitor connected in series or parallel.
terms.more: Also called a tuned circuit, because it favors one frequency.

terms.def: A device that combines several semiconductors and other components into one package.
